classification.difficultyReason: Interpret perpendicular compass directions, identify the hypotenuse and calculate a shorter side to two decimal places.

content.prompt: Amelia starts from a point $A$ and walks 6 km due south to $B$. Amelia then walks due east to a point $C$ which is 7 km from $A$. How far is $C$ from $B$? Calculate your answer in kilometres, correct to 2 decimal places.

answer.worked:
South and east are perpendicular, so triangle $ABC$ is right-angled at $B$, with hypotenuse $AC=7$ km. Let $x$ be the length of $BC$ in kilometres.
$$\begin{align*}x^2+6^2&=7^2\\x^2+36&=49\\x^2&=49-36\\x^2&=13\\x&=\sqrt{13}\\x&\approx3.61\end{align*}$$
Using the square-root table on printed page 206, $\sqrt{13}\approx3.61$. Therefore, $C$ is $3.61\text{ km}$ from $B$, correct to 2 decimal places.
